description:
Executive summary of Teleport access-control posture, coverage and control-plane assurance. Entry point for the Teleport dashboard set; every tile drills into an analyst-grade board.

Panel-by-panel reasoning, what was deliberately left off, and the validation history: see dashboards/teleport-executive.md.

panels.description:
**Percentage of human users holding privileged access standing, rather than earning it just-in-time.**

Confidence: **Measured** (Access Graph, current state).

Bot and system identities (`@...`, `bot-...`) are excluded from the denominator — including them dilutes the ratio with identities that are *supposed* to hold standing grants.

⚠️ No period-over-period delta: the Access Graph is point-in-time. Deltas arrive with the rollup sink.

⚠️ Small denominator on this cluster — read the trend, not the digit.

links.title: Drill down: Users — Standing Privileges & MFA

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT round(100.0
  * count(*) FILTER (WHERE (value->'properties'->>'standing_privileges')::int > 0)
  / NULLIF(count(*), 0), 1) AS "Standing Privilege %"
FROM nodes WHERE kind='identity' AND subkind='user'
  AND value->>'name' NOT LIKE '@%' AND value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'

panels.title: Standing Privilege Ratio (humans)

panels.description:
**Percentage of human users with an MFA device registered in Teleport.**

Confidence: **Approximate** — this is *device enrolment in Teleport*, which is NOT the same as MFA coverage.

⚠️ **Three known ways this understates reality:**
1. **SSO users** whose IdP enforces MFA upstream have no Teleport-registered device and are counted here as not-enrolled. On this cluster that is a real case, not a hypothetical.
2. Identities with the property absent entirely (unknown state) are counted as not-enrolled.
3. `weakest_mfa_device_kind` reports the *weakest* factor, so an all-OTP fleet scores 100%.

Bot and system identities are excluded from the denominator.

links.title: Drill down: Users — Standing Privileges & MFA

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT round(100.0
  * count(*) FILTER (WHERE value->'properties'->>'weakest_mfa_device_kind' NOT IN ('UNSET',''))
  / NULLIF(count(*), 0), 1) AS "MFA Enrolled %"
FROM nodes WHERE kind='identity' AND subkind='user'
  AND value->>'name' NOT LIKE '@%' AND value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'

panels.title: MFA Device Enrolled (humans)

panels.description:
**Percentage of *operator-created* roles that grant wildcard (`*:*`) access to some resource kind.**

Confidence: **Measured** (Access Graph, current state).

**Built-in roles are excluded**, and this matters: Teleport ships presets (`access`, `editor`, `requester`, `terraform-provider`, …) that hold wildcards *by design*. Counting them measures Teleport's defaults, not your policy. Roles are classified by the `teleport.internal/resource-type` label — `preset` and `system` are built-in; auto-generated `bot-*` roles are excluded too.

See the *Role Inventory by Origin* table below for the split.

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
WITH created AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT value->>'name' AS name, id
  FROM nodes WHERE kind='identity_group' AND subkind='role'
    AND coalesce(value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','') NOT IN ('preset','system') AND value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'
)
SELECT round(100.0 * (
  SELECT count(DISTINCT c.name)
  FROM created c
  JOIN edges e1 ON e1.from_node = c.id
  JOIN nodes a  ON a.id = e1.to_node  AND a.kind='action'
  JOIN edges e2 ON e2.from_node = a.id
  JOIN nodes rg ON rg.id = e2.to_node AND rg.kind='resource_group'
  WHERE rg.value->>'name' = '{"*":"*"}'
) / NULLIF((SELECT count(DISTINCT name) FROM created), 0), 1) AS "Wildcard Role %"

panels.title: Over-Permissioned Roles (created)

panels.description:
**Number of roles your team actually authored** — the surface area of policy you own and must review.

Confidence: **Measured** (Access Graph, current state).

Excludes Teleport `preset` and `system` roles and auto-generated `bot-*` roles. The full split is in the *Role Inventory by Origin* table below.

**This tile replaced a 'Dead Roles' ratio, which was removed as unsound** — it relied on `member_of` edges, and roles granted to SSO users through login rules produce no such edge, so live roles were reported as dead. See the spec for detail.

links.title: Drill down: Role Inventory by Origin

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(DISTINCT value->>'name') AS "Operator-Created Roles"
FROM nodes WHERE kind='identity_group' AND subkind='role'
  AND coalesce(value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','') NOT IN ('preset','system') AND value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'

panels.title: Roles: Operator-Created

panels.description:
**Every second factor Teleport supports, and which this cluster accepts.**

Confidence: **Measured** (Teleport API, via the usage exporter).

All three types are listed whether or not they are configured — an inventory, not just what happens to be on — so a type that is off is a visible gap rather than something inferred from an absence.

Colour reflects how much Teleport can actually vouch for:

- **WebAuthn — green.** The strongest factor Teleport verifies itself.
- **OTP — amber.** Accepted, but weaker than WebAuthn, which is available and unused.
- **SSO — blue, not amber.** SSO is *not a factor Teleport checks*. It delegates the entire MFA ceremony to the identity provider and accepts whatever the IdP enforces. That could be hardware keys and device trust (stronger than anything Teleport verifies on its own) or it could be SMS. **Teleport cannot see which**, so the honest reading is *unknown*, not *weak*. If SSO is in use, audit the IdP's own MFA policy — this tile cannot do it for you. Teleport's docs note the flexibility "presents the possibility of insecure misconfigurations". Enterprise-only, OIDC and SAML connectors only.

This layer is unreachable from any Grafana datasource: `cluster_auth_preference` is API-only, and the `auth_preference.update` audit event records that MFA changed, not what it changed to.

Three related questions, deliberately kept apart:
- **this tile**: which factors does the cluster *accept*?
- **MFA Device Enrolled**: have users actually *registered* one?
- **Session MFA Required**: is a fresh check demanded before privileged access?

Hardware-key policies (`HARDWARE_KEY_TOUCH`, `HARDWARE_KEY_PIN`) live on `require_mfa_type` rather than the second-factor enum and are not yet exported — a Phase 3b addition.

links.title: Drill down: Per-Role Session MFA Enforcement

panels.title: Second Factors — inventory of what Teleport supports

panels.description:
**Does the cluster require a fresh MFA check before a privileged session, rather than only at login?**

Confidence: **Measured** (Teleport API, via the usage exporter).

`require_session_mfa` at the cluster level. Roles can also set this individually — see the per-role breakdown on the Identity Security board, where the reference cluster has **0 of 35** roles enforcing it.

Login-time MFA proves who started the session. Session MFA proves who is using it *now*, which is what limits the value of a stolen session.

links.title: Drill down: Per-Role Session MFA Enforcement

panels.title: Session MFA Required (cluster)
Role Inventory — what we authored vs what Teleport ships

panels.description:
**Every role, split by who created it.**

Teleport ships roles of its own, and conflating them with yours makes every role-based ratio meaningless — `access`, `editor`, `requester` and `terraform-provider` hold wildcards *by design*, and most presets are unassigned on a normal cluster.

Classification uses the `teleport.internal/resource-type` label on the role:
- **preset** — shipped and created by Teleport on first start.
- **system** — Teleport-managed integration roles (Okta, AWS IC, access-approver).
- **bot-generated** — created automatically per Machine ID bot (`bot-*`).
- **operator-created** — authored by your team. **This is the only group the posture tiles measure.**

`Assigned (graph)` counts `member_of` / `impersonator_of` / `requester_of` edges. ⚠️ **It undercounts.** Roles granted to SSO users via login rules produce no graph edge, so a role can read `0` here and still be live — verified on this cluster, where `role-base` is assigned to an SSO user but shows no edge. Do not treat `0` as 'safe to delete'.

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
WITH roles AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (value->>'name')
    value->>'name' AS name, id,
    CASE
      WHEN coalesce(value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','')
           = 'preset' THEN 'Teleport preset'
      WHEN coalesce(value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','')
           = 'system' THEN 'Teleport system'
      WHEN value->>'name' LIKE 'bot-%' THEN 'Bot-generated'
      ELSE 'Operator-created'
    END AS origin
  FROM nodes WHERE kind='identity_group' AND subkind='role'
)
SELECT r.origin AS "Origin",
       r.name   AS "Role",
       (SELECT count(*) FROM edges e
          WHERE e.to_node = r.id
            AND e.kind IN ('member_of','impersonator_of','requester_of')) AS "Assigned (graph)",
       CASE WHEN EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM edges e1
         JOIN nodes a  ON a.id = e1.to_node  AND a.kind='action'
         JOIN edges e2 ON e2.from_node = a.id
         JOIN nodes rg ON rg.id = e2.to_node AND rg.kind='resource_group'
         WHERE e1.from_node = r.id AND rg.value->>'name' = '{"*":"*"}'
       ) THEN 'yes' ELSE '' END AS "Wildcard access"
FROM roles r
ORDER BY (r.origin = 'Operator-created') DESC, r.origin, r.name

Coverage & Adoption — are we getting what we bought?

panels.description:
**Resources enrolled in Teleport as a share of the known estate.** The gap is the shadow estate — the part of the environment where none of the other tiles apply.

Confidence: **Measured** numerator (Teleport API, via the usage exporter) ÷ **operator-supplied** denominator.

The numerator was previously the Access Graph's resource count. It agrees today, but the Access Graph is Enterprise-only, so sourcing from it denied this panel to OSS deployments for no reason. The exporter reads the same resources through the API and is also the billing-relevant definition.

⚠️ The denominator is the `known_estate_size` variable, maintained by hand — Teleport cannot know how big your estate is. Update it quarterly along with `known_estate_updated`; a stale denominator yields a confidently wrong percentage. Shows *Not configured* while it is 0.

**On the expression:** the `and on() (vector(...) > 0)` guard makes the query return nothing when `known_estate_size` is 0, so the tile reads *Not configured*. Dividing by 0 in PromQL yields `+Inf`, which Grafana renders as a real-looking value.
panels.title: Estate Coverage (estate as of ${known_estate_updated})

panels.description:
**Distinct human users with at least one session in the selected period.**

Bots are excluded — they do not count toward billable MAU and including them here would misrepresent adoption.

Confidence: **Approximate**. Derived by classifying audit events; `user_kind` is known to be inconsistent, so treat this as investigative rather than authoritative. The license portal remains the authoritative source.

Bot rule (matching the tracker): bot iff `user_kind` contains `bot` or equals `2`.

links.title: Drill down: Identity & Access — login and session activity

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(DISTINCT event_data->>'user') AS "Human Active Users"
FROM public.events
WHERE event_type IN ('session.start','db.session.start','app.session.start','windows.desktop.session.start','kube.request')
  AND event_time >= $__timeFrom() AND event_time <= $__timeTo()
  AND NOT (lower(coalesce(event_data->>'user_kind','')) LIKE '%bot%' OR event_data->>'user_kind' = '2')

panels.title: Human Active Users (period)

panels.description:
**Share of sessions by protocol over the selected period.**

Answers "did we buy a platform and deploy one protocol?" A healthy rollout broadens past SSH over time.

Confidence: **Approximate** (audit-event classification). Kubernetes sessions are `session.start` events carrying a `kubernetes_cluster` field, plus `kube.request`; SSH is `session.start` without one.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_type='session.start' AND event_data->>'kubernetes_cluster' IS NULL)  AS "SSH",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE (event_type='session.start' AND event_data->>'kubernetes_cluster' IS NOT NULL)
                      OR event_type='kube.request')                                                 AS "Kubernetes",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_type='db.session.start')                                             AS "Database",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_type='app.session.start')                                            AS "Application",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_type='windows.desktop.session.start')                                AS "Desktop"
FROM public.events
WHERE event_time >= $__timeFrom() AND event_time <= $__timeTo()

panels.title: Protocol Mix (share of sessions)

panels.description:
**Total resources Teleport protects.** This is the TPR figure billing is based on.

Confidence: **Measured** (Teleport API, via the usage exporter).

Read from the API rather than inferred from heartbeat gauges or audit events. Three independent sources agree on this cluster — the exporter, `teleport_connected_resources`, and the Access Graph — and `scripts/validate-dashboards.py` asserts the first two stay in agreement (C1).

A predecessor to this panel read a tracker table that had recorded 0 for a month after its credentials expired, while labelled *faithful*. If this collector fails the series is **withdrawn** and the panel reads *No data*; it will never show a zero it did not measure.
panels.title: Protected Resources (TPR)

panels.description:
**Protected resources by kind.**

Confidence: **Measured** (Teleport API, via the usage exporter).

Every kind is emitted including zeros, so a kind you do not use is a visible zero rather than a missing bar. Absence here means *not measured* — the collector withdraws its series on failure — which is deliberately different from a measured zero.
panels.title: Protected Resources by Kind

panels.description:
**Distinct human active users per calendar month.**

Confidence: **Approximate** (audit-event classification, bots excluded).

⚠️ The window shown is limited by audit retention, not by the dashboard's time range. This is *not* a 13-month trend until the rollup sink lands — read the x-axis, not the intent.

links.title: Drill down: Identity & Access — login and session activity

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  to_char(date_trunc('month', event_time), 'YYYY-MM') AS "Month",
  count(DISTINCT event_data->>'user')                 AS "Human Active Users"
FROM public.events
WHERE event_type IN ('session.start','db.session.start','app.session.start','windows.desktop.session.start','kube.request')
  AND event_time >= $__timeFrom() AND event_time <= $__timeTo()
  AND NOT (lower(coalesce(event_data->>'user_kind','')) LIKE '%bot%' OR event_data->>'user_kind' = '2')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Human Active Users by Month

panels.description:
**Session volume by protocol, per calendar month.**

The adoption story over time: a stack that broadens is a platform rollout, a stack that stays one colour is an SSH replacement.

Confidence: **Approximate** (audit-event classification).

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  to_char(date_trunc('month', event_time), 'YYYY-MM') AS "Month",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_type='session.start' AND event_data->>'kubernetes_cluster' IS NULL)  AS "SSH",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE (event_type='session.start' AND event_data->>'kubernetes_cluster' IS NOT NULL)
                      OR event_type='kube.request')                                                 AS "Kubernetes",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_type='db.session.start')                                             AS "Database",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_type='app.session.start')                                            AS "Application",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_type='windows.desktop.session.start')                                AS "Desktop"
FROM public.events
WHERE event_time >= $__timeFrom() AND event_time <= $__timeTo()
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Protocol Mix by Month
Control-Plane Assurance — can we still prove what happened?

panels.description:
**Three independent ways the audit record can lose evidence, over the last 7 days.** Target is zero on all three, so these are deliberately counts and not ratios.

- **Failed audit emits** — `audit_failed_emit_events`, a true counter. Events Teleport could not write.
- **S3 session-upload errors** — `s3_requests{result!="success"}`. Recordings that failed to reach the session bucket. A previous version of this panel claimed to cover S3 but queried no S3 metric.
- **Peak sessions pending upload** — `teleport_incomplete_session_uploads_total`.

⚠️ **`teleport_incomplete_session_uploads_total` is a GAUGE despite its `_total` suffix** (confirmed via Prometheus metadata, 2026-08-31). An earlier version of this panel wrapped it in `increase()`, which runs counter-reset logic over a value that legitimately falls every time an upload completes — producing an arbitrary number. It is now read with `max_over_time`.

⚠️ **Windowed by `$prom_retention`, not by the dashboard range.** Prometheus retention is a property of the cluster this is installed on, so the window is a dashboard variable rather than a hardcoded value. A range longer than retention would compute over whatever exists and present it as the longer period — the failure this variable exists to prevent.

Confidence: **Measured** (Prometheus).

links.title: Drill down: Ops Health — Audit Pipeline

panels.title: Audit Continuity — evidence integrity (${prom_retention})

panels.description:
⚠️ **Pinned to 7 days, not the dashboard range.** Prometheus retention on this cluster is `7d` (verified 2026-08-31). A `[90d]` window would silently compute over 7 days of data and present the result as a quarter — a green tile that means nothing. Raise Prometheus retention (or land the rollup sink) to widen this honestly.

**Average availability of Teleport's monitored targets over the selected period.**

The system that gates all production access was reachable this fraction of the period.

Confidence: **Approximate**. This is scrape-target availability (`up`), which is a proxy for service availability — it does not distinguish a scrape failure from an outage, and it carries no error budget. A true SLO with burn rate is planned as a Prometheus recording rule.

Requires a scrapeable Prometheus; absent where the diagnostics endpoint is not exposed.

list.description: Prometheus retention on THIS cluster. Every PromQL range selector on this dashboard is derived from it, so the panels can never claim a window the datastore does not hold. Set it to match `spec.retention` on your Prometheus (kube-prometheus-stack default is short). Raising Prometheus retention and then raising this widens the panels honestly.
list.label: Prometheus retention

list.description: How far back the Teleport audit backend actually holds events. This is a DIFFERENT and usually much longer clock than Prometheus retention — on the reference cluster the audit DB held 116 days while Prometheus held 7. Audit-sourced (SQL) panels use this; Prometheus panels use $prom_retention. Do not collapse them into one value.
